subject: Week 19: choking-hazard audit - everything goes in the mouth now
bodyText:
This week
Days 131-137 are the pre-solids consolidation week: tripod sitting with hands forward for 5-10 seconds, deliberate bring-to-mouth exploration of texture, babble strings with real intonation, and laughing at peek-a-boo. Rolling is possible or emerging - the CDC 2022 checkpoint is 6 months, so no rolling yet is within range. A few early movers rock on hands and knees; more typically that lands at 6-10 months.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Everything in the mouth - necessary developmental exploration, not a behavior to discourage. Supervise and control the floor instead.
- [low concern] 30-45-minute catnaps - common at this age and typically lengthening by 5-6 months. If he wakes content and the next wake window holds, the nap is doing its job.
- [monitor] Persistent inability to bear weight on his legs when held standing, or no rolling in either direction - worth a line in the 6-month visit notes.
- [call within 24h] Fever of 100.4F rectal or higher with reduced feeding, or acute illness onset with unusual irritability - same-day call.
- [call now] Fever of 102F rectal or higher, sudden-onset lethargy, labored breathing, or blue lips - 911 for breathing or color change.

Enrichment opportunities
- Walk every room at floor level this weekend: coins, batteries, magnets (neodymium sets are life-threatening if two are swallowed), small toy parts, pet food. Install outlet covers while you are down there - crawling typically starts at 7-10 months. AAP - Childproofing Your Home: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/at-home/Pages/Childproofing-Your-Home.aspx
- Prop him into supported sitting with toys in a semicircle and you as the backstop - 5-10-second tripod holds are the current working set. Offer a toy at midline and watch for the hand-to-hand transfer. AAP - Movement: 4 to 7 Months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-4-to-7-Months.aspx
- Restructure the day around three naps if the fourth is collapsing - wake windows run 2-2.5 hours at this age, and the last nap should end by 16:30-17:00 to protect an 18:30-19:30 bedtime. AAP - Baby Sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/default.aspx
- Keep the weekly SFPL Baby Rhyme & Play Time slot on the standing calendar - free, ticketed at popular branches, and the Cantonese session doubles as live L2 exposure; the infant program runs to 15 months. SFPL storytimes: https://sfpl.org/kids/kids/events/storytime-sfpl

Upcoming
- Day 168-182 (Oct 26-Nov 9, 2026): 6-month well visit - confirm it is booked. Bring the iron question if exclusively breastfed, the allergen plan, and sleep status.
- Sat Sep 26, 2026 (week 20): the day 140-200 participatory-music enrollment window opens - decision brief next week.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Uses voice to express joy and displeasure
  AAP window: day 120-210
  What to look for: Distinct vocalizations for different states — early affective communication.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-voice-for-joy/complete

- Rolls from back to tummy
  AAP window: day 120-210
  What to look for: Harder direction; requires more core and upper-body strength.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/rolls-back-to-tummy/complete

- Reaches for objects with one hand
  AAP window: day 120-210
  What to look for: Differentiation from earlier two-handed swiping — emerging hand preference is normal but unstable until ~age 3.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/reaches-with-one-hand/complete

- Pushes up with straight arms during tummy time
  AAP window: day 120-180
  What to look for: Full arm extension, chest off the floor. Builds toward sitting.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/leans-on-hands-tummy-time/complete

- Leans on hands to support self when sitting
  AAP window: day 120-180
  What to look for: Tripod sit. Precedes hands-free sitting by 1-2 months.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/sits-with-hand-support/complete
